name: Microsoft Dragon Copilot vs Nabla
title: Microsoft Dragon Copilot vs Nabla: Enterprise AI Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Microsoft Dragon Copilot and Nabla AI scribes for enterprise healthcare. See differences in EHR integration, multilingual support, and deployment.

summary.bottom_line: Both are enterprise-grade AI documentation platforms. Dragon Copilot offers the deepest US health system integration with Epic/Cerner, dictation, and GPT-4. Nabla excels in multilingual support (35+ languages), zero server-side data storage, and flexible EHR embedding via SMART on FHIR. Choose Dragon Copilot for US enterprise with Epic; choose Nabla for multilingual international deployments.

key_differences.data_privacy: Nabla (zero server storage) vs Dragon Copilot (Azure-hosted)
key_differences.ehr_flexibility: Nabla (SMART on FHIR) vs Dragon Copilot (deep Epic/Cerner)

sections.heading: Microsoft Dragon Copilot vs Nabla: Overview
sections.content: Microsoft Dragon Copilot and Nabla are both enterprise-grade AI documentation platforms, but with different strengths and geographic focuses. Dragon Copilot is Microsoft's unified clinical AI assistant combining ambient capture, Dragon Medical One dictation, and GPT-4—optimized for US health systems using Epic and Cerner. Nabla is a Paris-based platform with US operations, known for 35+ language support and a unique privacy architecture where patient data never touches Nabla's servers. Both serve 85,000-100,000+ clinicians but appeal to different deployment scenarios.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Both require enterprise/sales conversations for pricing. Dragon Copilot is estimated at $150-300+ per provider per month based on industry averages. Nabla historically offered individual plans around $119/month with enterprise plans at $299-399/provider/month. Neither publishes current public pricing. Dragon Copilot includes more bundled technology (dictation, GPT-4); Nabla's value is in multilingual support and privacy architecture. Both represent significant investments appropriate for enterprise deployments.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Dragon Copilot's unique advantages: Dragon Medical One dictation, GPT-4 generation, nurse documentation support (2026), HITRUST certification, and the deepest Epic integration. Nabla's unique advantages: 35+ language support for diverse patient populations, zero server-side data storage (data stays in browser), SMART on FHIR EHR embedding via Nabla Connect, and European headquarters with strong GDPR focus. For US English-only health systems on Epic, Dragon Copilot excels. For international or multilingual deployments, Nabla is superior.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your geographic focus and language needs:

recommendations.when: You're a US health system on Epic or Cerner, need dictation capabilities, want HITRUST certification, or need nurse documentation support
You serve multilingual patient populations (35+ languages), operate internationally, prioritize zero server-side data storage for privacy, or want flexible SMART on FHIR embedding
You're a large enterprise with complex requirements—both are proven at scale (85,000-100,000+ clinicians) and merit enterprise evaluation

faqs.q: Which is better for multilingual practices?
faqs.a: Nabla is significantly better for multilingual practices with 35+ language support including Arabic, Mandarin, Spanish, French, Hindi, and Vietnamese. Dragon Copilot is focused on US English-speaking deployments.

Dragon Copilot has deeper Epic integration with embedded workflows developed through Microsoft's healthcare partnerships. Nabla also integrates with Epic via SMART on FHIR and Nabla Connect, but Dragon Copilot's Epic relationship is more mature.

faqs.q: Does Nabla have dictation like Dragon Medical One?
faqs.a: No, Nabla focuses on ambient AI capture without traditional dictation. If you need voice dictation for reports or correspondence, Dragon Copilot with Dragon Medical One is the better choice.

Nabla's unique architecture means patient data never touches their servers—it exists only in the clinician's browser. Dragon Copilot processes data through Azure (with enterprise-grade security). For maximum data minimization, Nabla's architecture is distinctive.
